record.paper_title: A metal-insulator transition in 2D: Established facts and open questions
record.context_brief: Need for a quantitative Pomeranchuk-effect theory
record.original_question: Can the proposed Pomeranchuk-effect explanation for the metallic temperature dependence of the resistance and the giant positive magnetoresistance in strongly interacting two-dimensional systems be developed into a quantitative theory, rather than remaining only a qualitative account of the observations?

evidence.quote: The Pomeranchuk effect provides a qualitative explanation of all the major experimental observations; however, a quantitative theory is not currently available.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a strongly interacting two-dimensional electron (or hole) system at low carrier density, in the regime where the dimensionless interaction parameter r_s = (πn)^{-1/2}/a_B* (with n the carrier density and a_B* the effective Bohr radius) is large, so that Coulomb interactions dominate over kinetic energy. Such systems exhibit two prominent experimental signatures:

(i) a strong "metallic" temperature dependence of the resistivity ρ(T), where dρ/dT > 0 over a sizable temperature range below the Fermi temperature T_F, with ρ varying by a factor of several between T ≪ T_F and T ∼ T_F; and

(ii) a giant positive magnetoresistance under an in-plane magnetic field B_∥ that fully polarizes the electron spins, with ρ(B_∥)/ρ(0) growing by an order of magnitude or more before saturating at the spin-polarization field B_sat.

A qualitative scenario attributes both phenomena to an electronic analog of the Pomeranchuk effect: at low temperature (or low B_∥) the spin entropy of a nearly localized component of the electron fluid exceeds that of the itinerant Fermi-liquid component, so that increasing T (or aligning spins with B_∥) shifts spectral weight between localized and itinerant components, thereby raising the resistivity.

Problem. Develop a quantitative theory implementing this Pomeranchuk-effect scenario for a clean, strongly interacting 2D electron system at large r_s. Specifically, construct a model (with explicit Hamiltonian or effective free-energy functional, and clearly identified microscopic parameters) from which one can derive, with controlled approximations, closed-form or numerically computable predictions for:

(a) the full temperature dependence ρ(T, n) at B_∥ = 0, including the magnitude and position of the metallic dρ/dT > 0 regime;

(b) the in-plane-field magnetoresistance ρ(T, n, B_∥) for 0 ≤ B_∥ ≤ B_sat, including the saturation value ρ(B_sat)/ρ(0) and its dependence on n and T;

(c) the dependence of the apparent metal–insulator crossover density n_c on disorder, valley degeneracy, and material parameters,

in quantitative agreement (within stated error bars) with measurements on high-mobility Si-MOSFETs, p-GaAs, and n-SiGe two-dimensional systems. Does such a quantitative Pomeranchuk-effect theory exist?
artifact.status_search_result: A fully quantitative Pomeranchuk-effect theory of the metallic ρ(T) and giant in-plane magnetoresistance in strongly interacting 2D electron systems does not yet appear to be established. Recent work (2022–2025) develops phase-coexistence and renormalization-group scaling models capturing aspects of the behavior near the 2D MIT, and the Pomeranchuk-effect picture has been quantitatively realized in related platforms (magic-angle and multilayer graphene), but a controlled quantitative theory matching all major observations in Si-MOSFET / p-GaAs / SiGe 2DES remains absent.

status_evidence.title: Spin effect on the low-temperature resistivity maximum in a strongly interacting 2D electron system
status_evidence.snippet: Pomeranchuk effect predicted within a phase coexistence region between the Wigner crystal and a Fermi liquid; quantitative description still being developed.
status_evidence.claim: Pomeranchuk-effect-based explanation for low-T resistivity features in 2D remains at the level of phase-coexistence modeling rather than a complete quantitative theory.

status_evidence.title: Fluctuating magnetism and Pomeranchuk effect in multilayer graphene
status_evidence.snippet: Isospin Pomeranchuk effect in multilayer graphene where a fluctuating moment phase is entropically favoured over a symmetric Fermi liquid.
status_evidence.claim: Quantitative Pomeranchuk-effect modeling has progressed in graphene analogs, but not as a complete theory of the original 2D MOSFET/GaAs metallic behavior and giant magnetoresistance.

status_evidence.title: Fate of Pomeranchuk effect in ultrahigh magnetic fields
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of Pomeranchuk-type liquid-solid transitions of electrons in high magnetic fields.
status_evidence.claim: Active research in 2025 still treats the electronic Pomeranchuk effect phenomenologically in the 2D MIT context.
